correctness.rationale: PASS applies only to repairs/2/RESULT.md. The frozen substitution at lines 83–104 combines valid-block flags and ends with an identity AND without specifying the required inversion. Read literally, it outputs Ind(z) instead of 1−Ind(z); Wang–Wu §3.3 checks p(τ_d)=0, so every promised input then lacks an accepting certificate. Since Definition 3.8 also outputs zero on unpromised inputs, that literal substitution is constant zero, refuting its rectangle bound. The repaired circuit explicitly inserts a free NOT before the final AND, after computing the conjunction, with all padding before that final output. Independently, ripple additions cost at most 2(j+1) ANDs each; their tree sum is 4m−2k−4. The prefix comparator invariant gives the two inclusive threshold flags in 4(k+1) ANDs, plus at most one for their OR. Together with conjunction and the terminal AND this is at most 4km+2k²+2k<5km. For the repaired polarity, sequential enforcement of the multiplication constraints fixes the outputs, and the identity p≡fg fixes the whole degree-(2d−2) certificate uniquely and accepts it precisely on the promise. For d=5km the field has enough points and (2d−2)/2^(4k)<1/6; four shared evaluations and independent address sampling give the existing O(k log k) protocol, including error control when no address is valid. The 0-rectangle proof uses projection density and existence of an accepted certificate at the selected valid address. The 1-rectangle proof uses uniqueness and 4k(2d−1)>m/(8k). The repaired N_k=km+4km(2d−1), 8√40<51 and k≤log₂N_k give the stated explicit bound, and Wang–Wu Fact 2.1 and their RP-to-NP query simulation give the two communication lower bounds. The frozen verifier checks components and sample parameters, not the final acceptance polarity; it was inspected, not executed.
